v: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.

And again, he began to teach beside the sea, and the largest crowd is gathered to him. As a result, having gotten into a boat, he sat down on the sea, and the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.

Sometime later, Jesus again started to instruct people while he was next to the Sea of Galilee. A very large group of people assembled to hear him. Because {there were so many people}, he got into a boat on the sea and sat down {to teach}. All the people stood on the shore, by the water.
And He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said,
And he was teaching them many things in parables, and he was saying to them in his teaching, \*
Jesus began to use stories to instruct them about many things. As he was instructing them, he said, \*
“Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.
“Listen! Behold, the sower went out to sow.
“Listen to this: a farmer began to plant some grain seeds
And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
And it happened that as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
As he was scattering them over the soil, some of the seeds fell on the path. Then some birds flew down and ate those seeds up.
he was scattering them over the soil
he was scattering them over the soil
Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
And other fell on the rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it did not have deep soil. \*
Other seeds fell on shallow soil on top of a layer of rocks. Because they were growing in shallow soil, the seeds sprouted very quickly. \*
on top of a layer of rocks
on top of a layer of rocks
they were growing in shallow soil
they were growing in shallow soil
they were growing in shallow soil
they were growing in shallow soil
they were growing in shallow soil
But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
And when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
Then, the sun shone on the new plants and dried them up. Then, because they did not have good roots, the plants died.
Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.
And other fell into the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it did not give fruit. \*
Other seeds fell onto an area full of thorny plants. These thorny plants grew quickly and crowded out the grain plants. So, the grain plants did not produce a crop. \*
an area full of thorny plants
an area full of thorny plants
Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop— one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.
And others fell on the good soil, and it was giving fruit, growing up and being increased, and one was bearing 30, and one, 60, and one, 100.”

Finally, other seeds fell on fertile soil. They grew quickly, and they produced a crop. Some plants produced 30 {grains of wheat each}, others produced 60 {grains each}, and others produced 100 {grains each}.”
Then Jesus said, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
And he was saying, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!” \*
Then Jesus told them, “You should think carefully about what you just heard me say!” \*
You should think carefully about what you just heard me say
You should think carefully about what you just heard me say
You should think carefully about what you just heard me say
You should think carefully about what you just heard me say
You should think carefully about what you just heard me say
As soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about the parable.
And when he was alone, the ones around him with the Twelve were asking him about the parables.
Later, when no one else was with them, Jesus’ 12 representatives and some other apprentices asked Jesus to explain the stories he had told.
no one else was with them
no one else was with them
no one else was with them
He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,
And he was saying to them, “To you has been given the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to those, the ones outside, everything is in parables,
He replied, “God has revealed to you hidden things about his kingdom. However, I use only stories to instruct people who are not my apprentices.
so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’
so that, ‘Looking, they may look but may not see, and hearing, they may hear but may not understand, lest they might turn back, and it might be forgiven to them.’” \*

That way, {just as you can read in the Scriptures,} ‘They will look at things, but they will not really see them. They will hear things, but they will not learn from them. Otherwise, they would stop doing what is wrong, and God would forgive them.’” \*
they would stop doing what is wrong
Then Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?
And he says to them, “Do you not understand this parable? And how will you understand all the parables?
Then Jesus told his apprentices, “Unless you realize what that story means, you will not be able to realize what any of the other stories {that I tell} mean.
{In the story that I told you,} the seeds that the farmer planted represent the good news.
In the story that I told you
Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
Now these are the ones beside the road, where the word is being sown, but whenever they have heard it, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that was sown in them. \*
Some people are like the seeds that fell on the path. They hear the good news. However, as soon as they hear it, Satan comes and makes them forget the message that they heard. \*
Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.
And similarly, these are the ones being sown on the rocky ground, who, whenever they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy,
Other people are like the seeds that fell on shallow soil on top of a layer of rocks. When they hear the good news, they rejoice and quickly believe it.
shallow soil on top of a layer of rocks
shallow soil on top of a layer of rocks
But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
and they have no root in themselves, but are temporary. Then, tribulation or persecution having happened because of the word, immediately they are caused to stumble. \*

However, they are like plants without good roots, which do not live very long. In fact, when bad things happen or when people hurt them because they accepted the good news, they quickly stop believing it. \*
which do not live very long
which do not live very long
which do not live very long
Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,
And others are the ones being sown into the thorns. These are the ones having heard the word,
Other people are like the seeds that fell onto an area full of thorny plants. They hear the good news.
an area full of thorny plants
an area full of thorny plants
but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
and the worries of the age and the deceitfulness of riches and the desires concerning other things, entering in, choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

However, they continue to focus on things in this world. They try to become rich, even though being rich is not as helpful as they think it will be. Also, they desire many other things. When they do those things, it makes the good news ineffective, just as thorny plants crowd out the good plants and keep them from producing a crop.
even though being rich is not as helpful as they think it will be

Still others are like the seeds sown on good soil. They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop— thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold.
And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and receive it and bear fruit—one, 30, and one, 60, and one, 100.” \*

Finally, other people are like the seeds that fell on fertile soil. When they hear the good news, they believe it. They are like the plants that produced a crop. Some plants produced 30 {grains of wheat each}, others produced 60 {grains each}, and others produced 100 {grains each}.” \*
They are like the plants that produced a crop
Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?
And he was saying to them, “The lamp does not come so that it might be put under the basket or under the bed, does it? Is it not so that it might be put on the lampstand?

Then he told the people who were there, “People do not bring an oil lamp {into a house} in order to cover it with a basket or a bench. Instead, they put it on a lampstand {so that it shines brightly}.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.
For it is not hidden except so that it might be revealed, nor has it become secret except so that it might come into visibility.
Here is what I mean: some things are secret, but that is only because God will {eventually} let everyone know about them.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!” \*
You should think carefully about what you just heard me say!” \*

He went on to say, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.
And he was saying to them, “Watch what you hear. With the measure by which you measure, it will be measured to you, and it will be added to you.
Then he told the people who were there, “Make sure that you are listening carefully {to what I tell you}. How carefully you listen is how much God will enable you to learn and understand.
is how much God will enable
For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
For he who has, it will be given to him, and he who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” \*
God will reveal even more to people who already know some things {about the good news}. However, God will cause people who know very little {about the good news} to know nothing about it at all.” \*
Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
And he was saying, “Thus is the kingdom of God: As a man throws the seed on the ground,
Then Jesus said, “Here is what God’s kingdom is like: a farmer planted some seeds.
Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.
and he sleeps and gets up, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows—how, he himself does not know.
During a period of many days, those seeds started to grow. The farmer did not really know how they grew.
During a period of many days
During a period of many days
During a period of many days
During a period of many days
During a period of many days
During a period of many days
All by itself the earth produces a crop— first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.
The soil produces a crop of its own accord: first a blade, then a head, then a mature grain in the head.
The plants grew out of the ground on their own. First, the stalks grew. Then, the parts where the seeds would appear grew. Finally, the grain seeds grew in that part.
the parts where the seeds would appear grew
And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.
And whenever the fruit hands over, he immediately sends the sickle, because the harvest has come.” \*
As soon as the plants produced grain, it was time to harvest it. So, the farmer told people to cut down the plants and collect the grain.” \*
to cut down the plants and collect the grain
to cut down the plants and collect the grain
Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
And he was saying, “How will we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable will we put it?
Then Jesus said, “I would like us to consider together what God’s kingdom is like. I will use a story to make sure that we all understand it.
I would like us to consider together what
I would like us to consider together what
to make sure that we all understand
It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
{It is} like a mustard seed, which, when it has been sown in the soil, being the smallest of all the seeds on the earth,
Here is what it is like: someone plants a tiny mustard seed in the ground. This kind of seed is smaller than every other kind of seed in the world.
Here is what it is like
But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.
and when it has been sown, it grows and becomes greater than all the vegetable plants, and it makes large branches, so that the birds of the sky are able to nest in its shadow.” \*

Once someone plants it, the seed {sprouts and} grows quickly. The plant becomes bigger than every other kind of plant that people grow. It has big branches. In fact, birds can land in the shade it creates and make nests there.” \*
other kind of plant that people grow
With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.
And with many such parables he was speaking the word to them, just as they were able to hear;
Jesus used many stories like these to teach the good news to the people who were there. He taught them as much as they could understand.
to the people who were there
He taught them as much as
He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.
but he was not speaking to them without a parable, but by himself he was explaining everything to his own disciples. \*
He taught them by using stories only. Later, when no one else was with them, he told his apprentices what all the stories meant. \*
when no one else was with them
when no one else was with them
When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.
And he says to them on that day, evening having come, “Let us cross over to the other side.”
When it was evening on the same day, Jesus told his apprentices, “Let us go {by boat} to the other side of the Sea of Galilee.”
other side of the Sea of Galilee
After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.
And having left the crowd, they take him with {them}, as he was, in the boat, and other boats were with him.
Since Jesus was already in the boat, the apprentices sailed away with Jesus from the large group of people. Other people sailed with them in other boats.
Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.
And a great storm of wind happens, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filled. \*
Then there was a powerful windstorm! High waves were splashing into the boat and quickly filling it up with water. \*
But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?
And he himself was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. And they wake him up and say to him, “Teacher, is it not a concern to you that we are perishing?”

Meanwhile, Jesus was in the back part of the boat. He was asleep, with his head on a pillow. The apprentices woke him up and told him, “Instructor! We are going to die. You should be paying attention!”
Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence! He commanded. “Be still! And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
And awaking, he rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be silent! Be still!” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. \*
Then Jesus got up. He scolded the wind. He told the water, “Become still!” The wind stopped blowing, and everything became calm. \*
“Why are you so afraid? He asked. “Do you still have no faith?
And he said to them, “Why are you cowardly? Do you not yet have faith?”
Then Jesus told his apprentices, “You should not be so afraid. You should be trusting God by now!”
Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?
And they feared a great fear and were saying to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” \*
The apprentices became very afraid. They kept asking each other, “Who could Jesus be? The wind and the water do what he says!” \*
